$comment: Single Source of Truth for The Anchor brand. Generated 2026-03-22 from full codebase crawl of OJ-The-Anchor.pub. All AI agents, copywriters, and developers should reference this file for verified brand facts.

identity.name: The Anchor
identity.naming_rule: Use 'The Anchor Pub' when describing what the business is (SEO value), but use 'The Anchor' for general mentions (e.g. 'we at The Anchor love serving our community').
identity.type: Independent British village pub and restaurant
identity.heritage_statement: Part of the community since the 1800s
identity.detailed_heritage: A village pub since 1751 — nearly 275 years old. Stood before Heathrow existed; Heathrow grew from a grass airstrip in the 1940s.
identity.founding_year_note: RESOLVED 2026-03-22: Canonical year is 1751. Claims.json (1866), blog posts (1869), and footer ('since the 1800s') are all incorrect and should be updated.

descriptions.marketing: The closest traditional British pub to Heathrow Airport. Famous Sunday roasts, beer garden under the flight path, and FREE parking for all guests.
descriptions.footer: Your local pub in Stanwell Moor, serving the community with great food, drinks, and entertainment since the 19th century.
descriptions.pwa: Traditional British pub near Heathrow with quiz nights, hosted events & great food

parking.description: Free on-site parking for pub guests. No fees, no time limit while visiting. Level surface, close to entrance. CCTV and floodlit.

amenities: Free WiFi (throughout pub and beer garden)
Live sports on TV (terrestrial only: BBC/ITV/Channel 4)
Dog friendly (water bowls and treats provided)

accessibility.note: Guests are encouraged to call ahead if they would like to plan their visit.
accessibility.beer_garden_access_note: There are steps from the bar to the garden, but a ramp is available on request.

family_facilities.children_welcome_until: Always welcome — completely family friendly including dogs. No age cut-off.

dog_policy.treats: Dog biscuits in a jar near the door
dog_policy.on_lead: Must be kept on a lead at all times

beer_garden.flight_path: Directly under Heathrow's southern runway approach path
beer_garden.peak_spotting_times: Planes operate on a rotating weekly schedule — one week landings are overhead until 3pm, the next week from 3pm. The schedule alternates weekly.
features: Full food and drink service during kitchen hours
Free high-speed guest WiFi throughout the venue

nearby_nature.name: Staines Moor Nature Reserve
nearby_nature.description: Ancient SSSI grassland — never ploughed in 1,000+ years — with over 200 bird species.

nearby_nature.name: River Colne Footpath
nearby_nature.description: Bankside path south through open wetland countryside towards Staines Moor.

nearby_nature.name: King George VI Reservoir Path
nearby_nature.description: Fenced embankment causeway between two vast reservoirs; outstanding winter wildfowl.

nearby_nature.name: Staines Reservoir Causeway Path
nearby_nature.description: High-level path across twin Staines Reservoirs (built 1902); superb birdwatching.

nearby_nature.name: Lammas Recreation Ground & Church Lammas Lakes
nearby_nature.description: Restored gravel-pit lakes in Staines with wheelchair-accessible paths, cafe, and toilets.

nearby_nature.name: Colne Valley Trail / Colne Valley Way
nearby_nature.description: Long-distance greenway from Thames at Staines to Rickmansworth; passes through Stanwell Moor.

nearby_nature.name: Stanwell Village Walk (Surrey County Council)
nearby_nature.description: Official easy walk with 1.4-mile and 2.7-mile options; longer route reaches Staines Reservoir.

nearby_nature.name: Stanwell and Staines Moor Circular
nearby_nature.description: Signposted moderate circular walk (~2.5 hrs) past reservoirs, Staines Moor, and River Colne.

nearby_nature.name: Bedfont Lakes Country Park
nearby_nature.description: 73-hectare Local Nature Reserve with four lakes, wildflower meadows, woodland trails, and dog exercise area.

nearby_nature.name: Wraysbury Reservoir & Lakes
nearby_nature.description: Internationally important SSSI wetland; superb wildfowl including smew, goldeneye, and kingfisher.

nearby_nature.name: Wraysbury and Hythe End Gravel Pits
nearby_nature.description: 117-hectare SSSI of former gravel workings with open water, fen, wet woodland, and scrub.

nearby_nature.name: Runnymede & Ankerwycke (National Trust)
nearby_nature.description: Historic Thames-side meadows where Magna Carta was sealed; ancient Ankerwycke Yew; free access.

community_context.dining_room_history: Original conservatory built in 1995 for George and Alex Best's wedding reception. Replaced with new dining room extension, renovation started April 2024, ready for Euro 2024 (14 June). Features French doors to garden.
community_context.greene_king_partnership: Renovation funding supported by Greene King. Stanwell Moor Brew developed in partnership.

food_hygiene.maintained_since: 7 years (since taking over the pub in 2019)
food_hygiene.staff_qualification: All staff hold Level 2 Food Hygiene qualification
